html:
Spanish America was the part of the Spanish Empire in the Americas, which at its height ran from California and Florida to the tip of South America. The chart dates it from the conquest of Mexico in 1521 to Mexican independence in 1821.

Conquest came first. After the Caribbean islands, Hernán Cortés and his Indigenous allies took Tenochtitlan in 1521 (see Fall of Tenochtitlan), and Francisco Pizarro took the Inca Empire from 1532. Epidemics such as smallpox and the cocoliztli killed a large share of the Indigenous population in the 1500s.

The crown then built a government to hold it:

  • Viceroyalties: New Spain, ruled from Mexico City, and Peru, ruled from Lima; New Granada and Río de la Plata were added in the 1700s.
  • The Church: friars and bishops converted Indigenous peoples, and image cults like Our Lady of Guadalupe took root.
  • Silver: mines such as Potosí and Zacatecas, worked by forced Indigenous labour, made Spanish coins the world's money. The treasure fleets carried it to Seville, and the Manila galleons carried it to China.

Society was ranked by birth: Spaniards from Spain at the top, American-born Spaniards (criollos) below them, then mixed people, Indigenous communities and enslaved Africans. Critics like Bartolomé de las Casas attacked the abuse of Indigenous people from the start.

When Napoleon took Spain in 1808, the colonies began to govern themselves. The wars of independence from 1810, led by figures such as Simón Bolívar, left Spain with only Cuba and Puerto Rico by 1825. The Latin American republics took its place.
sum: Spanish America was the part of the Spanish Empire in the Americas, which at its height ran from California and Florida to the tip of South America. The chart dates it from the conquest of Mexico in 1521 to Mexican independence in 1821.
